scenario: A city parade features six floats — Amaranth, Birch, Cedar, Dahlia, Elm, and Fern — divided into two districts: the Riverside district and the Hillside district. Each district contains exactly three floats. Within each district, the floats march in a strict order: first, second, and third. The assignment of floats to districts and their marching order within each district are subject to the following conditions.

rules.description: Positions 1–3 = Riverside slots 1–3; positions 4–6 = Hillside slots 1–3.
Amaranth does not march third in Riverside.
Amaranth does not march third in Hillside.
If both Birch and Cedar are in the same district, Birch marches before Cedar.
rules.note: encoded as global before: Birch position < Cedar position — valid because same-district pairs are always consecutive integer ranges

rules.description: If Dahlia is in Riverside (positions 1–3), then Elm is in Hillside (positions 4–6).
Fern and Elm do not march in consecutively numbered positions.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of floats to marching positions, where positions 1–3 are Riverside and positions 4–6 are Hillside?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Riverside: Cedar 1st, Amaranth 2nd, Dahlia 3rd; Hillside: Birch 1st, Elm 2nd, Fern 3rd

choices.label: B
choices.text: Riverside: Cedar 1st, Birch 2nd, Fern 3rd; Hillside: Amaranth 1st, Dahlia 2nd, Elm 3rd

choices.label: C
choices.text: Riverside: Cedar 1st, Amaranth 2nd, Fern 3rd; Hillside: Birch 1st, Dahlia 2nd, Elm 3rd

choices.label: D
choices.text: Riverside: Cedar 1st, Dahlia 2nd, Elm 3rd; Hillside: Amaranth 1st, Birch 2nd, Fern 3rd

choices.label: E
choices.text: Riverside: Birch 1st, Cedar 2nd, Fern 3rd; Hillside: Amaranth 1st, Dahlia 2nd, Elm 3rd

explanations.correct: In choice C: Cedar is 1st in Riverside (satisfies the Cedar-at-position-1 rule). Amaranth is 2nd, not 3rd, in Riverside (satisfies the Amaranth-not-third rule). Fern is at position 3, Elm is at position 6 — not adjacent (satisfies the Fern-Elm not-adjacent rule). Dahlia is in Hillside (positions 4–6), so the Dahlia-in-Riverside conditional does not fire. Birch (4) is before Cedar (1) — wait, Cedar is in Riverside position 1, Birch is in Hillside position 4. Since they are in different districts, the Birch-before-Cedar rule only applies within the same district; here they are in different districts, so it is vacuously satisfied. All rules are satisfied.
explanations.A: Dahlia is in Riverside (position 3), triggering the conditional that Elm must be in Hillside. Elm IS in Hillside (position 5), so that is satisfied. However, Fern is at position 6 and Elm is at position 5 — these are adjacent, violating the Fern-Elm not-adjacent rule.
explanations.B: Amaranth is in Hillside 1st (position 4), and Elm is in Hillside 3rd (position 6). Fern is at position 3 and Elm at position 6 — not adjacent, fine. But Dahlia is in Hillside 2nd (position 5) and Elm in Hillside 3rd (position 6) — Fern at position 3 and Elm at position 6 are not adjacent. Let's check the Cedar-at-1 rule: Cedar is at position 1 (Riverside 1st) — satisfied. Now Birch is in Riverside 2nd (position 2). Birch at 2, Cedar at 1: Birch is NOT before Cedar (2 > 1). This violates the Birch-before-Cedar rule since both would be in the same district.
explanations.D: Elm is in Riverside 3rd (position 3). Fern is in Hillside 3rd (position 6). Positions 3 and 6 differ by 3 — not adjacent. Amaranth is in Hillside 1st (position 4). Birch is in Hillside 2nd (position 5). Dahlia is in Riverside 2nd (position 2). Since Dahlia is in Riverside, the conditional fires: Elm must be in Hillside. But Elm is in Riverside (position 3) — this violates the conditional rule.
explanations.E: Cedar is at position 2 (Riverside 2nd), violating the rule that Cedar must be at position 1 (Riverside 1st).

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cedar marches first among all floats in Riverside.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Elm marches second in its district.

explanations.correct: The rule explicitly states that Cedar marches first in Riverside (position 1). This is a fixed constraint — Cedar is always at position 1 in every valid solution. This must always be true.
explanations.A: Birch can appear in either district. In several valid solutions (e.g., Birch at position 2 = Riverside 2nd), Birch is in Riverside, but in others (e.g., Birch at position 4 = Hillside 1st), Birch is in Hillside. Not a necessity.
explanations.B: Fern can appear in either Riverside (position 3 in many solutions) or Hillside. In solutions such as Amaranth-2, Birch-4, Cedar-1, Dahlia-5, Elm-6, Fern-3, Fern is in Riverside. But in solutions where Fern occupies Hillside slots, this fails. Not necessarily true.
explanations.D: In several valid solutions Dahlia is in Riverside (positions 1–3), for example when Dahlia is at position 3 (provided Amaranth is not also at 3 — Amaranth is forbidden from 3, so Dahlia at 3 is fine, and if Elm is also placed in Hillside, all rules are met). So Dahlia need not always be in Hillside.
explanations.E: Elm can occupy any of several positions depending on the world. There is no rule fixing Elm to the second slot of any district.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following cannot be true?

explanations.correct: A rule explicitly states that Amaranth does not march third in Riverside (position 3). This is a fixed prohibition — Amaranth at Riverside 3rd can never be true regardless of how the other floats are arranged.
explanations.A: Birch can march second in Hillside (position 5) in valid solutions, for example: Cedar-1, Dahlia-2 or another float-2, Fern-3, Amaranth-4, Birch-5, Elm-6. This is possible.
explanations.B: Fern can march third in Hillside (position 6) in certain valid arrangements — e.g., Cedar-1, Elm-2, Amaranth-4... with a complete valid assignment placing Fern at 6. Not impossible.
explanations.C: Dahlia at Riverside 3rd (position 3) is permitted. The rule triggered by this placement is the conditional: Elm must be in Hillside. As long as Elm is placed in positions 4–6 and other constraints are met, this is a valid arrangement.
explanations.E: Elm can march first in Hillside (position 4) in solutions where Dahlia is in Hillside (so the conditional does not fire) and Fern is not at position 3 (so the non-adjacency rule is satisfied). This is possible.
